title: Session Honoring Don Woods
session_title: Memorial Session in Honor of Don Woods
authors_text: Santiago Faucher and Jason M. Keith
abstract: Session Honoring Don Woods Abstract This session honors Professor Don Woods who passed away in April 2013. Dr. Woods was a chemical engineering professor at McMaster University from 1964 to 2000 where he used innovative teaching methods and won many teaching awards (and three honorary doctorates from Queens, Guelph and McMaster). He wrote many books and papers, and gave workshops in various parts of the world. What you may not know about Dr. Woods is that he was also an artist, banjo player, square dancer, badminton player, builder, author, genealogist, and great reader. He enjoyed spending time at Kinlough, the family’s 200 acre vacation place in southern Bruce County, as well as travelling to many interesting destinations in retirement. This session will highlight reflections on the impact of Dr. Woods career. Speakers in this session include: - Angie Perna, NJIT - Phil Wood, McMaster University - Rich Felder, North Carolina State University - Scott Fogler, University of Michigan - Charles Petty, Michigan State University - Suzanne Kresta, University of Alberta - George Chase, The University of Akron

title: Cross Flow Filtration Hydrocyclones
session_title: Memorial Session in Honor of Don Woods
abstract: A cross flow filtration hydrocyclone (CFFH) combines the desirable attributes of a vortex separator and a filter barrier. By selecting an appropriate hydrophilic filter medium, a CFFH clarifier has the potential to produce a filtrate phase with a low concentration of a dispersed organic phase in a single stage. The CFFH concept addresses three traditional problems associated with current hydrocyclone separators for oil/water separation: 1) the loss of separation performance due to core flow reversal; 2) the loss of separation performance due to entrained oil in the sidewall boundary layer; and, 3) the loss of separation performance due to hydraulic turndown. The paper will discuss the efficacy of using a forward-flow CFFH and a reverse-flow CFFH for clarifying produced water on offshore platforms and elsewhere. Computational fluid dynamic (CFD-) methods are used to identify practical prototype designs and operating characteristics. “The Ubiquitous Hydrocyclone: Theory and Practice, C. A.
